translations.blog.5-common-problems-installing-a-natu:
An unbalanced ecosystem can lead to algal blooms and murky water

One of the biggest problems with a nature pool is that the ecosystem becomes unbalanced, which can lead to severe algal blooms and murky water. To avoid this, it's important to maintain a good balance between plants and microorganisms. Water-purifying plants like reeds and water lilies help filter the water naturally, and a pump can ensure that the water remains in motion. Since a natural pool lacks chemicals, it takes time for the ecosystem to stabilize, but with proper planning, you'll achieve crystal-clear bathing water.

Incorrect placement can lead to too much sun or shade

The placement of your natural pool plays a crucial role in water quality. Too much direct sunlight can lead to increased algal growth, while too much shade can hinder the growth of aquatic plants. Ideally, place the pool where it receives sun for a few hours a day but also some shading, such as from strategically placed trees or shrubs. Floating plants can also help create natural shading and thus reduce the risk of algal problems.

Leaks and poor insulation can cause major problems

If the pool is not sealed properly, water leakage can cause major issues. Many use the wrong materials or neglect sealing, leading to increased maintenance costs. To avoid this, you should use a rubber liner or special clay to create a secure seal. It's also important to check the soil conditions before you start digging and ensure that the pool's construction is stable. A careful installation from the start saves both time and money in the long run.

Poor circulation can lead to stagnant water and low oxygen levels

If the water in your nature pool does not circulate sufficiently, it can become stagnant and start to smell bad. Poor oxygenation can also negatively affect the ecosystem. To solve this, you can install a low-energy pump that keeps the water in motion. A small stream or waterfall can also contribute to natural oxygenation. Avoid building too deep areas where oxygen supply becomes too low, and ensure that water flow is evenly distributed throughout the pool.

Incorrect plant selection can lead to ineffective water purification

Not all plants work equally well in a nature pool, and if you choose the wrong varieties, the water can quickly become dirty as the plants do not filter out nutrients effectively enough. It's important to use plants like reeds, eelgrass, and water clover to purify the water. By combining floating plants with rooted aquatic plants, you achieve effective filtration. Also, ensure to choose plants that thrive in your climate and in the pool's various depths to ensure a long-term sustainable solution.
Understanding algae: nature's double-edged sword

Algae are a natural part of all aquatic ecosystems. They contribute to oxygen production and serve as food for fish and other aquatic organisms. However, when algae grow excessively, they can cloud the water and disrupt the balance in your aquatic environment, leading to green hues and unpleasant odors. Understanding the causes of algal blooms is the first step towards better control.

Common causes of algal growth

Nutrient imbalance: Excess nutrients, often from fertilizers or decaying organic material, can drive algal growth. This imbalance is often due to runoff, neglected debris, or overfeeding fish.

Lack of vegetation: Aquatic plants absorb nutrients and compete with algae. A lack of healthy plants can lead to increased algal blooms.

Sunlight: While some sun is good, too much direct sunlight can promote algae growth. Therefore, it is important to balance sunny and shaded areas.

Proven methods for algae control

Promote healthy aquatic plants

Using multiple types of aquatic plants is one of the most effective ways to combat algae. Native plants thrive in the local environment and help create a balanced ecosystem. Plants like water lilies, water hyacinths, and submerged plants provide shade and absorb excess nutrients, limiting algae growth.

Expert tips: Aquascape's product design team recommends a plant-to-water ratio of about 50% to effectively control algae while also beautifying the aquatic environment.

Use beneficial bacteria

Beneficial bacteria can help break down organic material and reduce the nutrients that algae feed on. These natural bacteria products are designed to restore balance and clarity to the aquatic environment.

Customer example: One of Faunapoolen's customers had recurring problems with algae in their koi pond. After consulting with a certified Aquascape contractor, they began using beneficial bacteria regularly, resulting in clearer water and healthier fish. The pond developed into a vibrant ecosystem with natural balance.

Regular maintenance routines

A simple maintenance routine can prevent algae before problems grow. By regularly removing debris, checking water levels, and monitoring water quality, you can keep your aquatic environment healthy and balanced.

Maintenance checklist:

  • Clean filters and pumps monthly.
  • Remove leaves and debris that accumulate in and around the feature.
  • Test water quality regularly for pH, ammonia, and nutrient levels.

Shade and reduce sunlight

Strategically placed plants, paving, or other fixed elements can create shade that reduces the risk of heavy algae growth. If your aquatic environment receives too much direct sunlight, a pergola or nearby trees can filter the sun's rays.

Choose the right filtration system

A high-quality filtration system is essential for clean and clear water. Advanced systems for aquatic environments can effectively remove excess nutrients and particles, reducing the risk of algal blooms.

Collaborate with certified Aquascape contractors

While these methods can make a significant difference in your aquatic environment, it may sometimes be best to seek help from certified professionals. Certified Aquascape contractors have the knowledge and experience needed to design, install, and maintain aquatic environments with care.

Why seek help from certified professionals?

  • Expertise in balanced aquatic ecosystems.
  • Access to high-quality Aquascape products specifically designed for effective algae control.
  • Ongoing maintenance that keeps the aquatic environment in good condition year-round.

Summary: enjoy a healthy aquatic environment

With the right algae control and maintenance, you can enjoy a beautiful aquatic environment without worrying about heavy algal blooms. Faunapoolen helps you create and maintain a harmonious outdoor environment that reflects nature's tranquility.

Ready to take care of your aquatic environment?

If you have problems with your aquatic environment or want to install a new one, book a design consultation with Faunapoolen. We will guide you through the process and ensure that the aquatic environment remains a beautiful and healthy part of your property for many years to come.
translations.blog.build.bodyHtml:
How does a nature pool work?

A nature pool works by mimicking natural processes to keep the water clean and clear. Instead of chlorine and chemical filters, biological filters and special plants are used that are effective in breaking down organic material and purifying the water.

A nature pool consists of two main parts: a swimming zone and a regeneration zone. The swimming zone is where you bathe, while the regeneration zone is where the purification process occurs. Water circulates between these zones using a pump. The regeneration zone is filled with gravel, sand, and aquatic plants such as reeds, irises, and water lilies. These plants act as a natural filter that breaks down dirt and improves water quality. A well-functioning nature pool requires that the regeneration zone is large enough and properly designed to handle the amount of water and organic material introduced.

Benefits of a nature pool

There are many benefits to having a nature pool. Firstly, it is completely chemical-free, making the water much gentler on the skin and overall health. This is especially important for children or individuals with sensitive skin who often have issues with chlorine in traditional pools. Nature pools are also environmentally friendly as they do not require chemical additives or frequent water changes.

Visually, nature pools are something entirely different from regular pools. They can be designed to resemble a natural pond and blend into the landscape in a way that traditional pools never can. Additionally, you can plant beautiful aquatic plants in the regeneration zone, creating an oasis of greenery. Operating costs are also low since the system is self-cleaning once properly installed. The combination of aesthetics, sustainability, and low operating costs makes a nature pool an attractive choice for many.

How to build a nature pool yourself

Building a nature pool yourself requires careful planning and understanding of how the system works. The first step is to choose a suitable location for the pool. A sunny spot is ideal as the sun promotes plant growth and improves the efficiency of the regeneration zone. Next, it's time to plan the design of the pool, including size and shape. The swimming zone and regeneration zone should be well-balanced, and the regeneration zone should be roughly the same size as the swimming zone to ensure optimal purification.

Once the design is complete, excavation work begins. Dig both the swimming zone and the regeneration zone to the correct depth, ensuring the ground is stable. Avoid areas with roots or stones that could cause problems. After excavation is complete, a waterproof membrane is installed to protect the pool from leaks.

The next step is to install biological filters and water pumps that keep the water circulating between the zones. It is important to choose the right equipment to ensure the system functions properly. After installation, it's time to plant the plants in the regeneration zone. Choose plants known for their purifying properties, such as reeds and irises. Plant them in the right quantity and placement to optimize purification. Finally, fill the pool with water and start the system. Keep in mind that it may take a few weeks for the plants to establish themselves and for the system to function fully.

Common mistakes when building a nature pool

Building a nature pool yourself is a comprehensive project, and it's easy to make mistakes if you lack experience. One of the most common mistakes is making the regeneration zone too small in relation to the swimming zone. If the zone does not have enough plants or gravel, it cannot purify the water properly, leading to cloudiness and imbalance in the system.

Another pitfall is poor drainage around the pool. If the ground is not properly prepared, water from the surroundings can flow into the pool, bringing soil and organic material that disrupts the system. Incorrect choice of plants is also a common cause of problems. If the plants in the regeneration zone are not suitable for the purpose, purification will not work, which may require you to redo the work. Finally, it is important that the membrane used for sealing is of high quality and installed correctly. Even small leaks can cause major problems and lead to costly repairs.

Cost to build a nature pool

Building a nature pool yourself can be cost-effective compared to hiring a professional installer, but it is important to understand the costs. Material costs for a smaller nature pool can start at around 50,000–100,000 kronor, but this depends on size, material choice, and what components you need to purchase. However, if you make mistakes that require repairs or rework, the costs can quickly exceed the budget.

Is it better to hire a professional?

While it is possible to build a nature pool yourself, it is not without risks. A single mistake, such as incorrectly sized regeneration zone or poor sealing, can lead to problems that are both time-consuming and expensive to fix. Professional installers have the experience and knowledge to eliminate these risks and create a sustainable and well-functioning nature pool from the start.

By hiring an expert, you can get help with everything from design and ground preparation to installation and choosing the right plants. The result is a pool that works just as it should and requires minimal maintenance. If you want to ensure that your nature pool becomes an investment that lasts for many years, it is a good idea to consider getting help from a professional. It can save both time, money, and worries in the long run.

At Faunapoolen, we are happy to help you realize your dream of a nature pool. We offer a free phone consultation where we go through your needs and concerns together. Whether you want to build the nature pool yourself or want us to handle the entire project, we can guide you to the right decision.

Contact us Contact us today to get started.
translations.blog.can-i-use-water-storage-solutions-w:
Understanding water storage solutions

Rainwater harvesting involves collecting, filtering, and storing rainwater for irrigation, ponds, or other needs on the property. The system can be customized to the location and reduce dependence on municipal water or traditional wells.

Benefits of using water storage solutions

Sustainable resource management

Water storage solutions allow you to collect and use rainwater, reducing dependence on municipal water. It saves water and helps manage stormwater runoff, which can reduce erosion and pollution.

Cost savings

Although the initial investment in a water storage system can vary, the long-term savings on water bills can be significant. With rising water costs, having your own water source can be financially advantageous.

Flexibility

The systems can be tailored to different needs and properties. Whether you want to irrigate a garden, fill a pond, or maintain a natural swimming pond, water storage offers a flexibility that traditional wells may not always provide.

Drought preparedness

In a world where climate patterns are changing, having a reliable water source becomes essential. A water storage system ensures that you have access to water during dry periods, keeping your landscape healthy and vibrant.

Rainwater collection systems

Rainwater harvesting involves directing rainwater from roofs or hard surfaces to storage tanks. The method is sustainable and effective for those who want to make the most of their water resources. According to Greg Wittstock, a leading figure in water landscaping, rainwater harvesting in outdoor environments can enhance both function and appearance.

If space is limited or if the solution needs to be discreet, the system can be adapted to the location. The AquaBlox system can store water without disrupting the garden's expression while still providing access to water when needed.

Before you choose a system: things to consider

Before investing in a water storage solution, you should consider the following factors:

Local regulations

Always check local regulations regarding rainwater harvesting and water storage systems. Some areas have specific guidelines that must be followed.

System size

Determine how much water you need to store based on your usage needs. This will help you choose the right system size and type.

Maintenance

Although water storage solutions are generally low-maintenance, regular cleaning and monitoring are needed to ensure water quality. Certified Aquascape contractors recommend a clear maintenance schedule to keep the system in good condition.

Integration with existing water features

Consider how the water storage will work alongside existing ponds, water features, or irrigation systems. A well-designed system enhances the garden while providing practical benefits.

Example: homeowners choosing water storage

Many homeowners have integrated water storage into their outdoor environments with great results. One customer in a residential area had restrictions on well drilling due to local regulations. By installing a rainwater harvesting system, they were able to both enhance their garden and significantly reduce their water bill.

The garden became an oasis with vibrant plants and a beautiful pond, sustained by collected rainwater.

Conclusion: a smart choice for sustainable living

Water storage solutions offer a practical and eco-friendly alternative when traditional wells are not viable. With the right system, you achieve sustainable landscaping, lower water costs, and better water management.

Ready to enhance your outdoor environment?

At Faunapoolen, we help you create an outdoor environment that meets your needs. Whether you want to install water storage, create a beautiful water feature, or explore other eco-friendly options, our experienced team is here to assist you.

Contact us to schedule a design consultation and start planning a sustainable oasis in your garden.
translations.blog.creating-harmony-intergrating-water:
Introduction

A well-designed water feature should feel like a natural extension of the surrounding landscape. Whether it's a pondless waterfall, a koi pond, or a bubbling fountain, careful planning, expert design, and a sustainable approach are required for the water to seamlessly blend into the outdoor environment.

This guide shows how water features can interact with the garden's existing elements and enhance both appearance and function. With the right placement, materials, and ecological balance, the water feature becomes the heart of the garden – attracting wildlife, improving air quality, and creating a soothing environment year-round.

Understand your garden before adding water

Before installing a water feature, it's important to assess the terrain, elevation changes, and existing vegetation in your outdoor environment. Key factors to consider include:

Topography

Sloping areas are perfect for waterfalls, while flat surfaces are better suited for still ponds or fountains.

Light conditions

Some aquatic plants require full sunlight, while others thrive in shade.

Soil type

Sandy soil drains quickly, while clay soil retains water. This affects how stable the water feature will be.

Existing plants & hard surfaces

Harmonizing water with paved paths, decks, or flower beds creates a cohesive whole.

Benefits of integrated water features

Aesthetic appeal

A water feature creates a natural focal point.

Environmental benefits

Supports biodiversity by attracting birds, frogs, and pollinators.

Microclimate regulation

Water helps cool the surroundings during warm months.

Stress reduction

The sound of flowing water promotes relaxation and mindfulness.

Choose the right water feature for your garden

1. Pondless waterfall: a natural cascade

Best suited for: Small gardens, sloping landscapes, and low-maintenance solutions.

Pondless waterfalls are ideal for those who love the sound of trickling water but want to avoid the maintenance of a traditional pond. The water circulates through a hidden underground reservoir, making it an eco-friendly and easy-to-maintain option.

2. Koi pond: a living ecosystem

Best suited for: Larger gardens, nature lovers, and vibrant outdoor environments.

A well-balanced koi pond combines aquatic plants, fish, and biological filtration. Aquascape Inc's BioFalls® filter creates a self-sustaining ecosystem with clear water.

3. Bubbling stone fountains: a smart solution for small spaces

Best suited for: Courtyards, patios, and urban gardens.

A bubbling stone or urn is a perfect solution for small areas. It provides the soothing sound of water without the need for extensive construction.

Sustainable design principles

A water feature should be integrated in an environmentally friendly way. Here are some sustainable solutions:

Recirculating water systems

Reduces water consumption by continuously reusing water.

Solar-powered pumps

Reduces energy consumption and operating costs.

Natural vegetation

Native plants around the water feature support local wildlife.

Rainwater harvesting

A sustainable way to replace water loss due to evaporation.

Customize your water feature

Material choices

Using natural stone, aged wood, or ceramics for an authentic feel.

Lighting effects

Discreet LED lighting enhances the atmosphere in the evening.

Seasonal adjustments

Winter preparations ensure sustainability in cold climates.

Summary: create your dream garden

A well-integrated water feature enhances the entire garden experience. By customizing size, placement, and materials to the existing environment, even a small installation can create a harmonious and inviting oasis.

Your next step

Do you know someone considering a water feature but has limited space? Share this post with them and help others discover how water can transform a garden.

Ready to create your own water feature? Contact us to start planning your project.
translations.blog.difference.bodyHtml:
What is a natural pool?

A natural pool, also called a biological pool or ecological pool, is an environmentally friendly alternative to a traditional chlorine pool. Instead of chemicals, natural purification methods are used where plants and microorganisms keep the water clean. It creates a pool without chemicals where you can swim without chlorine and enjoy a natural bathing place at home.

Advantages of a natural pool:

  • No chemicals – The water is biologically purified, making the bathing experience gentler for both people and the environment.
  • Healthier water – Perfect for sensitive skin and allergy sufferers who want to avoid chlorine.
  • Lower operating costs – No expensive chemical handling or energy-intensive filtration.
  • Naturally aesthetic – A natural pool blends into the garden and creates a beautiful, harmonious environment.
  • Sustainable choice – A sustainable pool that benefits both the ecosystem and your economy in the long run.
  • Less maintenance – Maintaining a natural pool requires fewer efforts than a traditional pool.

How does a nature pool work?

Instead of using chlorine to purify the water, a natural pool operates through biological filtration. Water flows through plant zones where specific plants and microorganisms break down dirt and nutrients. This means you can enjoy a pool without chemicals, just like in a natural lake.

Difference between a natural pool and a regular pool

The biggest difference between a natural pool and a traditional pool is the purification method. A regular pool requires regular additions of chlorine and chemicals to keep the water sterile, while a natural pool is based on a natural ecosystem. Both options have their pros and cons depending on your priorities.

Advantages of a traditional pool:

  • Quick and effective purification – Chlorine quickly kills bacteria and algae.
  • Temperature control – Easy to heat and use year-round.
  • Standard solution – There are many ready-made pool packages to choose from.

Disadvantages of a traditional pool:

  • Chlorine can cause skin irritation and eye discomfort, especially for sensitive individuals.
  • Higher operating costs as chemicals and advanced filtration are required continuously.
  • Less environmentally friendly as chlorine and other chemicals can negatively impact the ecosystem.

Cost of a natural pool – what should you consider?

Many wonder what the cost of building a natural pool is. Compared to a regular pool, the initial cost may be slightly higher, especially if you want a customized ecosystem and design. However, a natural pool often has lower operating costs since you avoid buying chlorine and other chemicals.

Maintaining a natural pool is also simpler and cheaper in the long run. Since the biological system takes care of itself, you don't need to spend as much time and money on water purification.

Building a natural pool – what should you consider?

If you are considering building a natural pool, it is important to think through both design and function. Natural pools can be designed in many different ways, from modern geometric shapes to more organic and pond-like solutions. Regardless of style, it is important to ensure good water flow and choose the right plants.

Here’s how you can build a natural pool:

  • Plan size and design – Do you want a modern pool or a more natural bathing area at home?
  • Choose the right plants – These act as natural filters and help keep the water clean.
  • Build a stable structure – A well-planned natural pool lasts for many years without major renovation needs.
  • Optimize water flow – The placement of filtration zones and plants plays an important role in water quality.

Is a natural pool the right choice for you?

If you want a pool without chemicals and a more natural bathing experience, a natural pool is an excellent choice. It is gentler on both people and the environment, requires less maintenance, and can save money in the long run. Additionally, it becomes a beautiful part of your garden and creates a sustainable pool where the ecosystem can interact naturally. By adding design elements like stone paving, wooden decks, or stylish lighting, a natural pool can also feel both luxurious and modern.

Regardless of which pool type you choose, it is important to plan carefully and select what best suits your lifestyle and needs. At Faunapoolen, we have expertise in both natural pools and traditional pools, and we are happy to help you find the best solution for you.
translations.blog.how-faunapoolen-helps-golf-clubs-ma:
Water is both an opportunity and a responsibility for golf clubs

At Faunapoolen AB, we know that good water management is not just about aesthetics. It also concerns playability, sustainability, and long-term economics. With several years of experience in designing and maintaining eco-friendly water features, Aquascape and Faunapoolen can provide ecological expertise to golf courses where water is important for both beauty and function.

Why golf clubs need help with water management

Water is both an asset and a risk on golf courses. A well-designed pond can frame a fairway, create strategic challenges, and store water for irrigation. But without professional maintenance, the same pond can quickly become a source of problems: algal blooms, unpleasant odors, unstable edges, and clogged irrigation systems.

Golf clubs should offer first-class experiences for members and guests. When a water feature is neglected, it affects playability, reputation, and long-term value. A murky pond by the ninth green or a flooded bunker after heavy rain not only looks bad but also signals a lack of quality and control.

This is where Faunapoolen comes in. Our philosophy is based on ecological balance. We don't just maintain water; we work with nature to enhance it. By combining design expertise, professional maintenance, and chemical-free solutions, we ensure that every pond, lake, and stream positively contributes to the golf course.

The consequences of neglected water features

A poorly maintained water environment is more than just a nuisance; it can become a real risk. Across Europe, golf courses that neglect ponds and streams often face recurring problems that become more expensive over time.

Neglected ponds often experience algal blooms, which not only ruin the course's appearance but can also pose health risks to wildlife and visitors. Streams that become blocked by sediment or debris can overflow after heavy rain, damaging fairways and pathways. Lakes can also silt up and lose capacity if not monitored, reducing their usefulness for irrigation during dry periods.

Once problems arise, solutions become more complex and costly. Emergency dredging, land reshaping, or drainage work can disrupt play for months and require significant investments. Clubs that allow recurring water damage to continue risk their reputation, as players expect well-maintained courses.

Hidden costs: insurance and liability

An often-overlooked aspect of poor water management is the financial burden arising from insurance claims. Recurring flooding of fairways, erosion at greens, or damage to bridges and pathways can force clubs to file repeated damage reports.

In the short term, insurance may feel like a safety net. But over time, repeated claims drive up premiums and can, in some cases, make it harder to obtain favorable insurance terms. The hidden cost slowly eats away at the club's budget year after year.

By investing in preventive water management with Faunapoolen, risks are significantly reduced. A well-maintained pond or properly constructed stream is less likely to cause damage during seasonal shifts and extreme weather, saving both money and worry.

Seasonal challenges in scandinavia

Golf courses in Scandinavia face unique stresses due to significant seasonal variations.

  • Winter freezing and ice expansion stress ponds and lake edges, which can cause cracks, collapses, or damage to pond liners.
  • Spring snowmelt and runoff create rapid flows in streams and can overload courses lacking proper flow control.
  • Summer droughts highlight how important irrigation ponds are when stored water becomes the course's lifeline.
  • Autumn storms bring heavy rains that test drainage systems and the stability of streams.

In this environment, golf clubs need more than routine maintenance. They need a partner who understands seasonal water dynamics and can design systems that work year-round. This is the expertise Faunapoolen provides, where eco-friendly Aquascape-inspired methods are combined with knowledge of Scandinavian conditions.

Faunapoolen's expertise: a team for water management on golf courses

At Faunapoolen, our services go far beyond simple pond cleaning. We work with a comprehensive solution for water management:

  • Design and improvement of ponds and lakes for both beauty and irrigation function.
  • Design of streams that manage seasonal flows without erosion.
  • Chemical-free filtration systems that provide fresh and clear water.
  • Long-term maintenance plans tailored to each course's needs.

When golf clubs choose Faunapoolen, they choose a partner with proven expertise and experience in creating improvements that last over time.

How to get in touch with our maintenance team

We believe that every golf course deserves water features that are as robust as they are beautiful. Whether your club has recurring algal issues, flooding, or wants to redesign its water systems for better sustainability, Faunapoolen's team is ready to help.

You can contact us directly at 0735406757 or via email at info@faunapoolen.se.
translations.blog.how-filtering-works-with-nature-poo:
Natural filtration system

Nature pools use a biofiltration system that mimics processes found in nature. Instead of chemical treatments, these pools use a combination of plants, gravel, and beneficial bacteria:

Plants

Aquatic plants, such as reeds and water lilies, absorb nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, preventing algae growth. The roots create an environment for beneficial bacteria that break down organic material.

Gravel and stones

The bottom of a nature pool is often covered with gravel and stones that act as a mechanical filter to capture debris and sediment.

Beneficial bacteria

These microorganisms help break down organic material and maintain water quality.

Circulation system

Nature pools often have a circulation system that pumps water through the filtration areas to ensure that the water is continuously filtered and purified.

Why nature pools are good for the environment

Environmentally friendly

Nature pools reduce the need for harmful chemicals, protecting the surrounding environment and preventing chemical runoff into nearby waterways.

Biodiversity

They create habitats for various plants and animals, promoting biological diversity and attracting birds and other wildlife.

Water conservation

Nature pools use less water than traditional pools, thus contributing to water savings.

Improved water quality

By filtering water naturally, these pools help reduce pollution and promote cleaner waterways, benefiting both wildlife and local communities. In summary, nature pools offer a unique and beautiful way to enjoy water while making a positive impact on the environment.

Summary

Nature pools offer a unique and beautiful opportunity to enjoy water while making a positive impact on the environment. Do you want your own eco-friendly oasis in your garden? Contact us today, and we will help you design and install a nature pool that suits your style and promotes nature.
translations.blog.pool-conversions.bodyHtml:
Do you have a neglected and lifeless pool that needs a new life?

In this article, we will go through the benefits, process, and inspiring real examples of how traditional pools can be transformed into natural ecosystems. We will also highlight projects from certified Aquascape contractors, a global network of skilled water landscape professionals trained to create these types of natural transformations.

Why convert a traditional pool?

Traditional pools require ongoing maintenance, chemical treatment, and energy-consuming filtration systems. Homeowners often face challenges such as:

  • High electricity and water consumption.
  • Contact with chemicals that can irritate eyes and skin.
  • Unattractive pool covers during the off-season.
  • A sense that the pool is disconnected from the surrounding nature.

A natural swimming pond, on the other hand, offers:

  • Chemical-free water purified by plants and beneficial bacteria.
  • Energy efficiency through smart circulation.
  • Increased biodiversity as the pond becomes a habitat for frogs, dragonflies, and birds.
  • Beauty year-round that transforms the garden into a living landscape.

What is a natural pool?

A natural swimming pond, also called an ecosystem pond, is designed to work with nature rather than against it. Unlike traditional pools that rely on chemicals, these systems function as a closed loop where the water is purified through natural biological processes. The pond is often divided into two main zones: a deeper swimming zone for bathing and recreation, and a shallower regeneration zone with aquatic plants that filter and oxygenate the water.

In addition to these zones, complementary systems help maintain clarity and balance. Skimmers and biological filters remove debris and support beneficial bacteria, while gravel beds provide surfaces for microorganisms to thrive. Aeration systems ensure that the water maintains proper oxygen levels. Together, these components create a self-sustaining ecosystem that operates much like a natural lake or stream, with clean and clear water year-round.

The conversion process step by step.

Here is an overview of what a typical project may include.

Assessment and planning.

  • Evaluate the existing pool's structure, concrete, and plumbing.
  • Develop a new layout with regeneration zones and any streams.
  • Consider location, sunlight, and surrounding landscape.

Demolition or reshaping.

  • Drain the pool and remove unnecessary connections and details.
  • Soften hard angles or reshape the bottom for a more natural expression.

Installation of filtration.

  • Excavate areas for intake bay, streams, and wetland filters.
  • Install Aquascape pumps and EcoBlox if pond-free elements are desired.
  • Add natural stone to give the old pool a more natural appearance.

Regeneration zone and planting

  • Cover the zone with gravel.
  • Plant aquatic plants such as water lilies, reeds, and oxygenating underwater plants.

Filling and commissioning

  • Fill the pond with water.
  • Allow the ecosystem to stabilize, which can take about two weeks depending on size.

Final details

  • Add edge plants, lighting, and social areas such as fire pits or patios.
  • Introduce fish if it suits the project.

Real transformations from certified Aquascape contractors

Atlantis Water Gardens (New Jersey, USA)

Greg Wittstock, founder of Aquascape, often showcases work from leading certified contractors like Atlantis Water Gardens. One of their notable projects was a complete conversion of a rectangular chlorine pool into a kidney-shaped ecosystem pond with a waterfall and a large regeneration zone. The project demonstrated how even restrictive pool shapes can be reinterpreted with creative design.

"We took a pool that was falling apart and turned it into a paradise. The family now swims with koi, frogs, and turtles, and they don't miss chlorine for a second," says Atlantis co-founder Jack Chernick.

Living Ponds (Oregon, USA)

Living Ponds converted an older garden pool into a multi-level ecosystem with stream beds and wetland filtration. By reusing large parts of the original plumbing and adapting the concrete shell, they were able to reduce both costs and waste.

"We believe in building with nature, not against it. This transformation created an educational habitat for the homeowners' children," said the project manager.

Premier Aquascapes (Indiana, USA)

Premier Aquascapes conducted a large-scale pool conversion on a rural property. The project included rainwater harvesting and a swimming zone fed by a waterfall. They used components from Aquascape's Signature Series to ensure reliability and longevity.

"Our goal was to create a recreational area that felt like a mountain spring. We used native plants to ensure the pond thrived with minimal maintenance."

The examples showcase the passion and innovation that certified Aquascape contractors bring to each project, where ecological knowledge is combined with craftsmanship and artistic sensibility.

Environmental benefits

Switching from a traditional pool to a natural ecosystem pond offers many benefits:

  • Water savings: less evaporation and no need for draining for chemical balancing.
  • Lower carbon footprint: less energy use compared to electric filters and heating.
  • Support for pollinators: attracts bees, butterflies, and other beneficial insects.
  • Biodiversity: creates habitats for amphibians, birds, and aquatic species.

How does maintenance work?

Many assume that natural ponds require more maintenance, but when designed correctly, they are often easier to manage than traditional pools. Faunapoolen and other certified contractors offer seasonal maintenance plans that may include:

  • Removal of leaves and debris.
  • Pruning plants and seasonal maintenance.
  • Maintenance packages monthly, bi-monthly, or annually.

translations.blog.small-features-for-small-spaces.bod:
The power of water in a small space

Even small gardens can have great character with the right water features. A compact fountain, mini-pond, or pond-free waterfall can create calm, movement, and a natural focal point without taking over the space.

The right placement makes small water features feel larger

Water has a natural ability to make even small spaces feel larger by drawing the eye and creating a calming atmosphere. For those with a small garden or patio, a water feature can enhance the experience, improve air quality, attract beneficial wildlife, and create a personal sanctuary.

Key benefits:

  • Aesthetic appeal – A well-placed water feature creates a natural focal point and adds depth and movement.
  • Relaxation and stress relief – The sound of flowing water dampens city noise and creates a sense of calm.
  • Wildlife – Even a small fountain can attract birds and pollinators, contributing to local biodiversity.
  • Cooling effect – Water features help regulate temperature during warm months and provide natural cooling.
  • Eco-friendly solutions – Modern constructions focus on sustainability with recirculating pumps and low energy consumption.

Choosing the right water feature for small spaces

Pond-free waterfall

Perfect for small spaces. A pond-free waterfall creates the same atmosphere as a traditional water installation, but without the maintenance of a stagnant pond. The water flows over natural stone and disappears into a hidden reservoir, making it an excellent option for those who love the sound of running water but have limited space.

Koi pond

A small pond with koi or aquatic plants can be as compact as 1.5–2 meters in diameter, making it ideal for patios and smaller gardens. These self-sustaining ponds require minimal digging and can even be built above ground with a sleek stone frame.

Fountains and urns

If space is very limited, a bubbling stone fountain or a ceramic urn fountain is a perfect alternative. The water circulates in a hidden reservoir, making the solution both low-maintenance and energy-efficient.

Eco-friendly solutions: sustainable choices

To keep your water feature environmentally friendly, you can choose solutions such as:

  • Recirculating systems – Reduce water consumption with pumps that continuously reuse water.
  • Solar-powered pumps – Reduce energy consumption and operating costs.
  • Native plants – Plant local species around the water feature for better water retention and biodiversity.
  • Rainwater harvesting – Use natural rainwater to refill the system when possible.

Customize for your garden

Every small garden is unique, and good planning ensures that the water feature blends naturally into the outdoor environment. This is especially important to consider:

  • Garden layout and size – To ensure proportional placement.
  • Light and shadow conditions – Choosing plants and materials that thrive in specific environments.
  • Material choices – Using natural stone, ceramics, or metal to match your aesthetic vision.

Next steps: realize your vision

If you dream of a peaceful oasis in your small garden, it's time to explore the possibilities. Whether it's a rushing, chemical-free waterfall, a charming mini pond, or an elegant bubbling fountain, the right water feature can transform your garden into a relaxing and beautiful place.

Do you know someone considering a water feature for their small garden? Share this post with them and help others discover how water can create tranquility in the outdoor environment.

Ready to create your own water feature? Contact us to start planning your design.
translations.blog.sports-stars-natural-ponds.bodyHtml:
A new wave of health in elite homes

Unlike traditional pools, natural ponds use biological filtration systems, wet zones, and Aquascape® technology to keep the water crystal clear – without chlorine or harsh chemicals. These eco-friendly systems create a self-sustaining water environment that blends into the landscape while promoting recovery, relaxation, and well-being.

Athlete stars leading the way

David Beckham made headlines when he received permission to build a natural eco-pool on his estate in the UK. The pool is designed to use collected rainwater and wetland filtration, reflecting a growing interest among celebrities in sustainable health solutions with low environmental impact.

Shaquille O’Neal took it a step further – he installed a 22 x 15 meter koi pond with a 21-meter-long waterfall, wetland filter, sandy beach, and more. The project, carried out in collaboration with Aquascape Inc., became a groundbreaking example of natural pond construction.

Logan Paul, YouTuber and now sports personality, had a viral koi ecosystem built in Los Angeles – complete with urn fountains, wooden bridges, and lush aquatic life. His pond was also developed by Aquascape's elite team.

Even football stars like Neymar Jr. are building custom water environments for privacy, health, and rest – far from the spotlight, but perfectly aligned with their performance needs.

Cold water baths meet natural design

Athletes are aware of the benefits of cold water baths: improved blood circulation, reduced inflammation, and faster muscle recovery. A natural swimming pond offers these benefits without the sterile, clinical feel of an ice bath. Imagine stepping into a cold, clean waterway with natural stone underfoot and birdsong in the air.

Combine this with an outdoor sauna, rainwater-fed showers, and a deck for breathing exercises or yoga – and you have the ultimate recovery environment right outside your door.

Purposeful real estate investment

Natural swimming ponds are not just about well-being – they are also a wise long-term investment. These systems:

translations.blog.why-you-should-get-a-natural-pool.b:
Chemical-free swimming

One of the biggest advantages of a natural pool is that it is completely free from chemicals. Traditional pools use chlorine and other chemicals to keep the water clean, which can irritate both skin and eyes. Natural pools, on the other hand, use biological filtration, often with the help of aquatic plants, to keep the water clear and safe. This makes them ideal for families, especially those with small children or individuals sensitive to chemicals.

Low maintenance

Many assume that natural pools require extensive maintenance, but these ecological pools are actually low-maintenance in the long run. The ecosystem in the pool takes care of cleaning the water, which means less work and no expensive chemicals to add. While some initial installation and seasonal care are required, ongoing maintenance is minimal compared to traditional pools.

Environmentally friendly option

A natural pool is a sustainable choice for environmentally conscious homeowners. By using plants, sand, and biological filters to purify the water, you reduce the need for energy-intensive filtration systems. Additionally, these pools use much less water since there is no need for continuous draining or chemical balancing, which is great for water conservation.

Aesthetically pleasing

Natural pools often blend seamlessly into their surroundings and resemble tranquil ponds or small lakes. They can be designed to complement your garden with stone formations, waterfalls, and aquatic plants. The result is a pool that feels like a natural part of your garden rather than an artificial structure. This enhances the beauty of your outdoor space and increases property value.

Enjoyment year-round

Natural pools offer benefits year-round. In summer, they provide a refreshing place to swim, while in colder months, they can transform into a peaceful pond or be used for invigorating cold baths.

Cost-effective in the long run

Although the initial cost of building a natural pool may be higher than that of a traditional pool, the long-term savings make it worthwhile. Since you won't need to buy chemicals or expensive filtration systems, your maintenance costs will be significantly lower. Over time, you save money while enjoying a beautiful and eco-friendly bathing area.

Health benefits

Swimming in a natural pool is about more than just clean, chemical-free water. The calm and natural environment, with plants and water in harmony, helps lower stress levels and promotes increased well-being. During the cold months in Sweden, the natural pool offers a perfect opportunity for cold baths, something to enjoy even on dark winter days. Cold baths strengthen the immune system, improve blood circulation, and contribute to mental health. Additionally, the environment around the pool attracts wildlife such as birds and butterflies, creating a vibrant ecosystem in your garden.

Customization options

Natural pools can be designed in various styles, from minimalist and modern to rustic and natural. Whether you want a sleek, clean design or a pool that mimics a forest pond, there are endless customization options. You can also adjust the size and shape to fit your garden, making a natural pool a versatile option for any homeowner.

Conclusion

Switching to a natural pool is an investment in both your health and the environment. With benefits like chemical-free swimming, low maintenance, and a beautiful, eco-friendly design, it's easy to see why so many choose to transition to a natural solution. Whether you're concerned about sustainability or just want a pool that looks and feels more organic, a natural pool offers the perfect balance of luxury and nature.

By choosing a natural pool, you not only create a place for swimming — you enhance your home, conserve resources, and support a healthier lifestyle. Want your own eco-friendly oasis in your garden? Contact us today, and we will help you design and install a natural pool that fits your style and promotes nature.

translations.site.editorial.packageHelp: Packages are a starting point. You can leave the choice open.
translations.site.editorial.optionalChoicesBody: Choose what you already know. We can work out the rest together.
translations.site.editorial.contactHelp: Your name, email and location are needed for the brief. Phone and preferred contact time are optional.

translations.site.editorial.notesHelp: For example, how you would like to use the space and when you would like to begin.

translations.site.testimonials.brita-build.quote: Faunapoolen has built a wonderfully beautiful nature pool that fits perfectly into the surroundings of my house on southern Gotland. They have been very friendly and professional and have handled the challenges that arose during the process in a way that inspired confidence.
translations.site.testimonials.brita-life.context: On life with the nature pool
translations.site.testimonials.brita-life.quote: We have really enjoyed the pool, and the grandchildren loved it too and used it a lot.
translations.site.testimonials.patrik-garden.quote: Extremely happy with the garden work Ben and his team carried out. We had a fairly clear idea of how we wanted the final result to look. By listening to our wishes and also suggesting improvements, the final result exceeded our expectations.

translations.site.aquascape_projects.0.body: A pond at Aquascape’s headquarters, built together with contractors from across North America.
translations.site.aquascape_projects.1.builder: Diego Asturias and Dan Peterson, Fontana Ponds & Water Features
translations.site.aquascape_projects.1.body: A recreational pond with a zipline across the water, featured in Aquascape’s profile of its 2021 Artists of the Year.
translations.site.evidence_copy.certificationBody: We plan and build your pool using Aquascape technology, and help you maintain it.
translations.site.evidence_copy.certificationDetail: Certified Aquascape Contractor is Aquascape’s own certification programme, with training in building and maintaining water features. Faunapoolen is responsible for your project and your contact throughout the work.
translations.site.evidence_copy.technologyTitle: Built by Faunapoolen. With Aquascape technology.
translations.site.evidence_copy.technologyBody: Pumps keep the water moving. Filters catch debris, and microorganisms remove nutrients that can otherwise feed algae. We size the system for your pool.
translations.site.evidence_copy.technologyCare: Remove leaves and debris, and check the water level and circulation. You receive a plan showing what needs to be done throughout the year.
translations.site.evidence_copy.videoCaption: Image and film: Aquascape. An international example of the technology, not a Faunapoolen project. The film is in English.
translations.site.evidence_copy.networkTitle: Water features in the Aquascape network
translations.site.evidence_copy.networkBody: See how other builders use Aquascape technology in these two projects.
translations.site.evidence_copy.caseBody: Explore a nature pool on Gotland through photographs and films of the finished setting.
